title: Pinnacle verification questions and answers
description: Answers match the visible questions on the verification page. Source scope and limitations remain part of each answer.

questions.question: What is PinnacleAI® GPT-OS licensed for?
questions.answer: The supplied MD-5 lists PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 as a Class B, non-diagnostic developmental-support device. Its scope is tied to the named device, version, intended use and premises; it does not establish diagnostic authority or guarantee clinical outcomes.

questions.question: Are an MD-3 application and an MD-5 licence the same?
questions.answer: No. MD-3 is an application for a manufacturing licence. MD-5 is the issued manufacturing licence. The original application is reviewed; Class B is recorded on the issued MD-5. The separate issued classification decision copy was not available for inspection.

questions.question: What do the BIS and ISO records establish?
questions.answer: They describe specified management systems and the activities and locations within their scope. They do not establish the effectiveness of every intervention or promise a particular outcome for a child.

questions.question: Does a research protocol prove external validation?
questions.answer: No. A protocol describes planned methods. The AbilityScore external-validation record here is a protocol; completed results and their limitations are needed before treating that study as completed validation.

questions.question: Does one credential cover every Pinnacle centre?
questions.answer: No. Match the named institution and premises on each document. This collection contains all 52 workbook centres and 53 distinct HFR identifiers across the workbook and certificate copies. Eight district summaries are separate; these are not counts of verified active centres.

questions.question: Who can help with a correction or a current document?
questions.answer: Contact Gokul Rao at care@pinnacleblooms.org or 9100 181 181. Include the record title, reference number and source date so the relevant document can be located.

questions.question: What does Pinnacle’s 2.7 billion+ data-point figure mean?
questions.answer: The September 2026 company handout reports 2.7 billion+ structured platform records, based on database rows/events with a 17 July 2026 cutoff. Examples include session entries, assessment observations and technique ratings. The number is not a count of unique children, independent trial observations or verified AI-training examples.

questions.question: Does this establish the world’s largest child-development dataset?
questions.answer: No comparable worldwide ranking is established. For example, CentralReach reports over 5 billion clinical and financial data points, using a different counting basis. A valid comparison would need common definitions, dates, populations, data quality and permitted uses.

questions.question: Does the MD-5 licence approve the entire child-development lifecycle?
questions.answer: The MD-5 names PinnacleAI® GPT-OS v1.0.0 and defined non-diagnostic functions for ages 0–12. The broader BIS schedule lists software processes and developmental-support modules across the journey. These instruments establish different scopes; neither guarantees outcomes or certifies global exclusivity.

questions.question: Do WHO, UNICEF, CDC, NICE or UNESCO endorse Pinnacle?
questions.answer: No endorsement is established by the references on this page. Their guidance explains why monitoring, coordinated support, caregiver participation and inclusion matter. Pinnacle’s own documents must separately establish what Pinnacle provides.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Pinnacle developmental pathway?
questions.answer: Pinnacle’s purpose is to help children grow toward self-sufficiency and participation in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations each child needs. Its tagline is “Every child deserves a wonderful life.” The described approach connects ability measurement, child-specific planning, coordinated intervention, everyday practice, tracking, correction and reassessment. Individual outcomes vary.

questions.question: What do 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills mean?
questions.answer: Pinnacle describes these as different layers of its developmental framework: 17 domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, with 591 observations and AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. The totals belong to Pinnacle’s architecture, not a WHO-defined numerical hierarchy. Individual plans select relevant priorities. The earlier Whitebook used 344 skills across six domains; validation of an earlier version should not be automatically transferred to the newer framework.

questions.question: How do daily practice and monthly review connect?
questions.answer: The company sources describe 7–9 daily techniques selected for the child’s programme, human feedback through the Fusion tracking and correction module, and monthly AbilityScore refresh. The care team should explain the child-specific goals, practice guidance, review schedule and any adjustments. This is a programme description, not a guaranteed outcome.

questions.question: How do ICD-11, ICF, ICHI and SNOMED CT relate to PinnacleAI®?
questions.answer: Pinnacle’s dossier describes architecture and mappings using WHO’s ICD-11, ICF and ICHI, alongside SNOMED CT terminology from SNOMED International. Their roles are health information, functioning and participation, interventions, and consistent clinical meaning. Correct implementation can support interoperability; an item-by-item mapping audit was not supplied. Alignment is separate from endorsement, clinical validation and the licensed device’s intended use.

questions.question: Does Pinnacle focus on a diagnosis or on everyday-life goals?
questions.answer: Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need. These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition.

questions.question: Is PinnacleAI® certified as sovereign-grade or authorised worldwide?
questions.answer: The reviewed documents do not establish a sovereign-grade certification or worldwide market authorisation. Pinnacle describes an architecture intended for population-scale developmental support. A specific deployment needs documented local control and governance, validated interoperability, applicable permissions, operational capacity and evidence of performance for that population. MD-5 and BIS provide the particular scopes shown in their records.

questions.question: Are parents and caregivers named in the MD-5 intended use?
questions.answer: Yes. The MD-5 annexure states that PinnacleAI® GPT-OS is intended to assist parents, therapists, educators and caregivers through developmental ability measurement, readiness tracking, progress forecasting and adaptive therapy-plan support for ages 0–12. This explicitly includes family users of the licensed software. It does not confer professional therapist credentials or register homes as therapy centres; worldwide exclusivity has not been established.
